input.question: What happens to a person's debt when they are the last person of a family line and die?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't matter if you have family or not, debt cannot be inherited. If you do have debt when you die, your creditors can take from your estate to pay it off. If your estate is not large enough to pay the whole debt, the debt just goes away.

response.prediction: When the last person in a family line dies, any debts that this person owed become part of their estate. If the estate does not have enough money or property to pay off all the debts, the debts usually go unpaid. In most cases, creditors cannot collect from family members unless they also guaranteed the debt. The remaining debt is often forgiven, and the estate is closed. However, if the person had valuable assets, those might be sold to pay the debts before any inheritance goes to anyone else.
